title: Accounts Administrator
company: Capital Outsourcing Group Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Administrator

Join a growing team and play a key role in keeping the finances running smoothly.

Salary: £30,000 per annum

Full-time Permanent Monday-Friday, 40 hrs

We're looking for a highly organised and detail-focused Accounts Administrator to join a busy finance team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, takes pride in getting things right and thrives in a role where accuracy, organisation and teamwork really matter.

You'll play an important part in supporting the day-to-day finance function, working across accounts payable, customer accounts, payments, reconciliations and general financial administration.

What you'll be doing

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing purchase invoices and credit notes
- Reviewing supplier statements and ensuring invoices are received and processed accurately
- Supporting the management and collection of outstanding customer balances
- Setting up new customer and supplier accounts
- Processing employee expenses
- Preparing and making supplier payments
- Handling incoming finance-related queries by phone and email
- Processing payments securely over the phone
- Posting bank transactions using accounting software
- Managing the finance team inbox and ensuring queries are dealt with promptly
- Supporting the release of orders where payment requirements have been met
- Providing general finance administration and support to the wider team
- Taking on additional duties and projects as required

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who is:
- Experienced in a Financial Administrator, Accounts Assistant or similar role
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working with financial information and deadlines
- Confident using accounting systems and Microsoft Office
- Enjoys working in a fast paced and busy environment
- Reliable, proactive and able to manage competing priorities
- A positive team player who is happy to get stuck in

Previous experience using SAP or similar business/accounting systems would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

Why join us?

This is more than a processing role. You'll become an important part of a collaborative finance team and have the opportunity to develop your skills across a broad range of financial activities.

We offer:
- £30, 000 annual salary
- 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays
- Company pension
- On-site parking
- A supportive team environment
- Opportunities to develop your finance experience

The role

Job title: Accounts Administrator

Salary: £30,000 per annum

Contract: Full-time, Permanent

Hours: Monday-Friday, 40 hrs

Working arrangement: Office-based

COG LTD are acting as an employment agency.

title: Accounts Assistant 20 hrs Part time
description:
Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity in the Pocklington area? Do you enjoy working in a varied finance role where no two days are quite the same? Are you someone who takes pride in keeping things organised, spotting the detail that others miss and getting stuck in to help the wider team?

If so, this Accounts Assistant job in the Pocklington area could be exactly what you're looking for.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a successful and growing manufacturing business with a friendly, down-to-earth culture. Working closely with the Finance Manager, you'll become an important part of a small finance team, supporting the day-to-day running of the accounts function while helping the business through an exciting transition to a new finance system. This is a hands-on role where your initiative, organisation and willingness to muck in will be valued just as much as your finance experience.

What the Accounts Assistant job involves

As the Accounts Assistant, you'll provide support across a variety of finance activities, including:

Managing the sales ledger, raising invoices and ensuring customer accounts are accurate.

Chasing outstanding payments and carrying out credit control activities professionally over the telephone.

Processing purchase ledger invoices and reconciling supplier statements.

Investigating and resolving invoice and account queries.

Supporting purchasing administration and maintaining accurate records.

Assisting with goods received documentation and ensuring paperwork is completed correctly.

Maintaining accurate financial records using the company's accounting systems.

Supporting the finance team during the implementation of a new ERP system, including data migration and checking information for accuracy.

Producing reports and maintaining spreadsheets using Microsoft Excel.

Working closely with colleagues across different departments to resolve queries and ensure the smooth running of the finance function.

Supporting month-end activities and providing general accounts administration as required.

Skills required

We're looking for someone who enjoys taking ownership of their work and isn't afraid to investigate problems or suggest improvements. You'll ideally have:

Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Purchase Ledger or Sales Ledger role.

Experience of both sales ledger and purchase ledger processes.

Credit control experience with confidence speaking to customers over the telephone.

Excellent organisational skills with strong attention to detail.

The ability to prioritise your workload and work independently using your own initiative.

Strong communication skills and a friendly, approachable manner.

Good Microsoft Excel skills.

Experience using Sage would be advantageous, whilst knowledge of SAP Business One would be highly desirable, although training will be provided.

A proactive, positive attitude and a willingness to support colleagues whenever needed.

Someone who enjoys working as part of a close-knit team and will fit naturally into a friendly office environment.

Other information

Part time, permanent position

20 hours per week

Tuesday to Thursday: 9:00am - 2:00pm

Friday: 8:30am - 1:30pm (early finish every week)

Auto-enrolment pension

Cash healthcare plan

Employee discounts on company products

Free on-site parking

This vacancy is being advertised through KD Recruitment Limited who are operating as an Employment Agency.

Due to the volume of applications we receive, if you have not heard from us within two weeks, please assume you have not been shortlisted for this particular role.

KD Recruitment Limited is committed to a policy of equal opportunities in relation to job applications and is also committed to protecting your personal data. If you would like to read our Privacy Policy, please visit our website at where you will find all the information you need to know about how we will use and process your personal data.

You can also follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and LinkedIn for up-to-date vacancies and other helpful information.

title: Commercial Property Legal Secretary/Assistant - York
description:
Commercial Property Legal Secretary
Location: York, North Yorkshire
Salary: £26,000 - £33,000, depending on experience
Hours: 9:00am - 5:00pm, Monday to Friday
Contract: Permanent, Full-time
Working Pattern: Office Based

Are you an experienced Property Legal Secretary or Legal Assistant looking for a new opportunity in York?

We are recruiting for a Commercial Property Legal Secretary to join the property team of a well-established law firm.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with a strong legal secretarial or administrative background who already has experience supporting fee earners within Property Law.

While direct Commercial Property experience would be advantageous, candidates who have supported fee earners within Residential Conveyancing, Real Estate or another property-focused legal department are also encouraged to apply.

The Role

Working closely with solicitors and other fee earners, you will provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support across a varied Commercial Property caseload.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support to Property Law fee earners
- Preparing, formatting and amending legal correspondence, reports and property documentation
- Opening, maintaining and closing client and matter files
- Liaising professionally with clients, solicitors, agents, lenders and other third parties
- Managing diaries, appointments, meetings and key dates
- Handling telephone calls, emails and correspondence efficiently
- Updating the firm's case management system and maintaining accurate records
- Assisting with Land Registry documentation, searches and property-related administration
- Preparing documents and correspondence relating to commercial property transactions
- Supporting fee earners with the day-to-day progression of matters
- Maintaining confidentiality and ensuring a consistently high standard of accuracy
- Providing wider administrative support to the Commercial Property team when required

About You

Previous experience supporting fee earners within Property Law is essential for this position.

You may currently be working as a Commercial Property Legal Secretary, Real Estate Legal Secretary, Property Legal Assistant, Conveyancing Legal Secretary or experienced Property Legal Administrator.

Direct Commercial Property experience would be particularly welcomed, although applications are also encouraged from candidates with a strong Residential Property background who are interested in moving into Commercial Property.

You will also need:
- Strong legal secretarial and administrative skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- The ability to manage a busy workload and competing priorities
- Confidence communicating with clients and professional third parties
- Strong Microsoft Office and case management system skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- A professional, organised and proactive approach
- The ability to work effectively as part of a busy property team

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Property Legal Secretary to join a busy Commercial Property team and further develop their career within Commercial Real Estate and Property Law.

Interested? Apply today or get in touch for a confidential discussion.

title: Paralegal

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confidence handling financial information and maintaining accurate records.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively as part of a team.
- Proactive, practical, and client-focused approach.

- High standards of client care, with empathy and understanding for clients who may be experiencing difficult circumstances.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary
- Realistic targets
- Wellbeing support
- Vibrant social scene
- Comprehensive benefits package including pension, life cover, enhanced maternity and paternity pay, health cash plan, staff discounts, competitive holidays (plus a day off for your birthday!), and a cycle to work scheme

title: Team Administrator
company: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: A fantastic part time (15 hours) opportunity has arisen for a conscientious and dynamic administrator to join one of our close-knit and supportive Community Mental Health Teams (CMHT), here in York. The North CMHT is based in Huntington House and provides community-based support to people aged between 18 and 65 years old who are experiencing challenges with their mental health. Huntington House is nestled to the west of Monks Cross, is a short walk away from the Community Stadium and Vanguarde Shopping Park. It is on the outskirts of York City Centre just inside the ring road (North), benefits from free on-site parking and is easily accessible by car, bus and bicycle. As a member of this small and friendly team, you will work in an open plan office on the second floor of the building. This floor is also home to other community mental health teams and is an area of high activity; no two days are the same. If you are looking for a new challenge, enjoy variety in your work and are looking to be part of a team striving to make a difference, we will welcome your application for this role. Whilst having previous experience in an administrative role is essential, NHS or other health care experience is not. We are first and foremost looking for individuals with a passion for people, customer service experience, extensive organisational skills, an interest in working in a health care setting and a 'can do' attitude. This role is at the heart of a dedicated and caring team and is a pivotal role in the day-to-day operations. As part of the administration team you will work closely with the medical secretary, Consultants and Nursing colleagues, supporting them in ensuring that high standards are maintained and they have everything they need to provide the best possible care for the service users. We are looking for someone who feels comfortable multi-tasking in a busy environment, can communicate confidently, is thorough and takes pride in their work, can build strong working relationships with a variety of people, can prioritise their workload and work to deadlines. The following responsibilities are examples, please refer to the attached Job Description for the complete picture. With a starting salary of £25,760 pro rata, per annum, a generous NHS pension scheme, a fantastic annual leave package (27 days annual leave plus bank holidays) and access to other NHS staff benefits and discounts, it is fair to say that this job has a lot to offer. And, its not just the NHS pay scale and benefits that we offer that make joining our organisation an excellent choice, there are many training and development opportunities available, giving you the opportunity for career progression. All staff have regular 1-2-1s, quarterly supervision meetings and an annual appraisal, which provides lots of opportunity for discussion around achievements, challenges and aspirations. Staff recognition is very important to us; we work closely with colleagues to support development, the staff voice, and to recognise teams and individuals through our Greatix and Star Award schemes; highlighting the outstanding work being done every day. We recognise that Administrators are professionals and are a valuable asset to our organisation. We understand that they have a key role in the support and delivery of our services and that their contribution helps us in achieving our aim of consistently providing safe and high quality care for our service users. The kind of care we would want for ourselves and for our loved ones. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role.
